title: Strandwise prefetch adapters for FlashAttention
content:
Summary:

This note sketches a lightweight, modular approach to prefetch coordination for paged KV when using FlashAttention-style fused kernels. The idea is to treat long sequence generation as multiple "strands" (cohorts of tokens that will be processed together across time) and provide small adapter kernels that prefetch page ranges and synchronize KV hydration with FlashAttention launches without blocking the main host thread. Goal: reduce tail latency from on-demand KV page faults while preserving high utilization of FlashAttention kernels and keeping code changes localized to the kernel launch/dispatcher layer.

Motivation and background:
- Observed problem: when a request touches cold KV pages (paged-KV), stall time is dominated by device memcpy and page population. Naive prefetchers either overfetch and waste memory or block the launch pipeline, increasing latency for nearby requests.
- FlashAttention kernels are most efficient at high occupancy and contiguous batch shapes. Any prefetch logic should preserve the tiled launch shapes and avoid fragmenting warps.
- Many previous sketches focus on coarse-grained cohorting (cohort-prefetch, subpage-cohorts). This doc explores a strandwise model that is finer-grained and fits interleaved generation patterns seen in chat workloads (interleaved tokens from multiple conversations).

Core concept: strandwise prefetch adapters
- Strand definition: a strand is a small schedule unit representing a sequence of token indices that will be processed together across next N steps. For a chat workload with M concurrent conversations, each conversation contributes one or more strands depending on token variance.
- Adapter idea: insert a tiny adapter kernel per CUDA stream (or per stream-group) that: (1) inspects upcoming attention indices for the strand; (2) issues async page prefetch commands (cudaMemcpyAsync/copy engine hints) for required KV pages; (3) records metadata in a lightweight device-side bitmap or ring; (4) returns quickly so the dispatcher can continue launching compute kernels.
- The adapter is intentionally small (< 2KB of registers, < 1 microsecond in warm-run time) and should not perform heavy memory copies; it issues prefetches that are handled by the DMA engine or host staging buffers.

Integration with FlashAttention fused ops:
- FlashAttention expects contiguous Q/K/V memory layout and benefits from prefetching contiguous pages. The adapter computes page ranges per head-block and emits prefetch batches aligned to the largest common page size (e.g., 2MB huge pages if available, else 64KB subpages).
- To avoid fragmentation, the adapter groups prefetches by GPU L2-set affinity when possible (heuristic based on address bits). Grouping reduces cross-warp coherence pressure during FlashAttention loads.
- The dispatcher can consult the adapter's device ring to decide whether to launch a high-occupancy FlashAttention variant (aggressive register usage) or a lower-occupancy but more tolerant variant (uses fewer registers, higher shared memory) when prefetches aren't ready. This creates an implicit latency-utility tradeoff at launch time.

Scheduler heuristics (host + device cooperative):
- Strand priority: strands are tagged with priority buckets (interactive, batch, background). Interactive strands get earlier adapter scheduling and are less likely to be grouped with incompatible tokens.
- Staleness window: adapter keeps a timestamp (tick) per strand. If a prefetch is older than T ticks, it's reissued. T is calibrated from microbenchmarks (initial value: 4 generation steps).
- Backpressure: if adapter queues exceed threshold (measured in in-flight prefetch ops), dispatcher reduces concurrency for background strands and favours prefetched interactive strands.
- Cost model: simplest model is tokens-prefetched / prefetch-ops-cost. Run periodic profiling to estimate average memcpy latency for a range of page sizes, then compute expected savings per strand. This is used to evict or skip prefetches for low-benefit strands.

Device data structures (minimalist):
- Strand registry (device-resident ring buffer): circular array of structs {strand_id, head_page_range_start, head_page_range_end, tick, flags}. Keep it small (power-of-two length 512).
- Prefetch batch queue: small device queue of page descriptors. Adapter appends to it; DMA engine consumes via separate kernel or host-side poller. Stored as two 32-bit words (addr_hi, addr_lo).
- Prefetch bitmap (optional): coarse 1-bit per page to avoid duplicate prefetches. Stored per-stream-group.

Kernel adapter pseudocode (host / device split):
- Host: before launching FlashAttention for a strand, enqueue adapter kernel to the same stream (low-latency). Adapter returns quickly. After adapter completes, either immediately launch FlashAttention or check device ring for completion bits if a synchronous guarantee required.
- Device adapter kernel: read small token index array (passed as kernel arg pointer), map indices to page ranges, append page descriptors into prefetch queue with atomic operations, bump strand tick.

Prefetch mechanism options (ranked):
1) GPU-to-GPU DMA with cudaMemcpyAsync into preallocated device page cache region (fastest when supported by HW/driver).
2) Host staging with pinned buffers + cudaMemcpyAsync (compatible fallback).
3) Unified memory advisor prefetch calls (cudaMemPrefetchAsync) for platforms with good UM support.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Keep adapter kernel footprint small: avoid large locals and looping over heads; prefer bit-twiddling to compute page indices.
- Avoid blocking atomics heavy contention: use per-stream-group queues to reduce cross-stream atomics.
- Security: ensure page addresses are validated against per-tenant allocation table (private deployments). Metadata writes should use bounds-checked atomics.
- Memory pressure: adapt prefetch aggressiveness to per-GPU free list. If free memory dips below threshold, stop prefetching background strands.

Microbench plan (short experiments to calibrate parameters):
1) Measure adapter latency vs varying strand token counts (1..8) and head counts (8..32). Goal: adapter kernel <= 1.2x host-side branch overhead.
2) Prefetch batch size vs memcpy throughput: test (4KB..2MB) pages to find sweet spot given our drivers.
3) Launch time decision payoff: benchmark launching aggressive FlashAttention vs conservative variant when prefetch incomplete. Collect 99p tail.
4) Multi-tenant noise tests: run 32 strands with interleaved hotspots and measure eviction/reissue churn.

Operational and rollout checklist:
- Feature gate behind runtime config: strandwise_prefetch_enabled, prefetch_threshold, page_group_size.
- Start in Canary region with Synthetic replay of chat workloads.
- Add tracing tags for each adapter invocation, page-prefetch op, and final KV-hit vs miss counts. Expose in console per-route breakdown.

Open questions and TODOs:
- How well do device-side rings scale with 1000s of simultaneous strands? Might need hierarchical fanout mapped to SMs.
- Prefetch correctness under model parallel KV sharding: need to ensure adapter maps global indices to correct shard and issue prefetch to the owner device instead of local DMA.
- Should adapter support speculative compression-aware prefetch (request compressed pages and decompress on device)? Pros/cons TBD.
- Evaluate tradeoff of issuing prefetch from host vs device (device issues are faster but harder to orchestrate across GPUs).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a sketch intended for discussion with kernel and scheduling owners. I tried to keep the runtime changes localized to the dispatcher and prefetch subsystem; most model kernels (FlashAttention) remain unchanged except for optional low-latency variant selection.
- If we like the approach, next steps: prototype adapter kernel, implement device ring + host poller, run perf matrix on p4d/p40/p100-equivalent infra.

Appendix: rough ASCII timeline for a single strand
- t0: dispatcher enqueues adapter_kern(stream S)
- t0+ε: adapter appends two page descriptors into prefetch queue
- t0+δ: host enqueues dma_kern or polls queue to issue memcpyAsync
- t0+δ+memcpy: DMA completes; device page cache populated
- t0+Δ: dispatcher launches FlashAttention; kernel runs with low stalls
